match.reason: No point in the bank covers recruiting staff from inside or outside the business; the closest, resources needed to start, only mentions planning for staff and does not teach recruitment.

draft.title: Recruitment
card: Recruitment is the process of finding people to fill a job vacancy. A business can look inside itself or outside it.

filling the job with a current employee, by promotion or transfer. It is usually cheaper and quicker, and it rewards staff who have worked well. It can also leave a gap in the job the employee came from.

filling the job with someone from outside the business, often through job advertisements or recruitment agencies. It brings new ideas and skills, and it gives a larger pool of applicants. It usually costs more and takes longer.
A business chooses between the two by weighing cost, time, the skills it needs and the effect on current staff.
draft.remember: Internal recruitment is cheaper and rewards staff. External recruitment brings in new ideas.

a.q: Which is a reason a business might recruit internally?
opts: It rewards current staff for good work
It brings new ideas into the business
It gives the largest pool of applicants
It avoids leaving a gap in another job
a.why: Promoting a current employee shows other staff that good work is noticed. New ideas and a larger pool of applicants come from external recruitment. Internal recruitment does not avoid a gap, because the employee's old job must be filled.
a.clue: Think about what staff see when a colleague is promoted.

b.q: Harbour Fitness in Newcastle has run the same classes for years and sales have stalled. The owner wants fresh ideas for the new manager's job. Which approach suits this aim best?
opts: Recruit externally, as outsiders bring new ideas
Recruit internally, as it costs less and is quicker
Recruit internally, as it rewards loyal staff
Recruit externally, as it avoids any training costs
b.why: The owner's aim is fresh ideas, and a person from outside brings a different view of how to run the business. Internal recruitment is cheaper and quicker, but that does not meet this aim. External recruitment does not avoid training costs, since the business may still need to train a new person.
b.clue: Match the method to what the owner wants most, not to the cheapest option.

a.best: It rewards current staff for good work

b.best: Recruit externally, as outsiders bring new ideas

problems.detail: Why (a) says the employee's old job 'must' be filled. The card only says internal recruitment 'can' leave a gap, so the why overstates it.
The remember line says internal recruitment 'is cheaper'. The card says it is 'usually cheaper', so the remember line drops the qualifier and overstates the claim.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and have one clear answer each. Why (a) says the old job 'must' be filled where the card says 'can', and the remember line drops the card's 'usually'.
